description_en: Bhindyaḥ Phalcā stands on Bhindyaḥlāchi Square, on the western side of the street leading from the Patan Palace to Cyāsal. According to an inscription, it was originally dedicated to Lord Bhīmasena and today it is an important space wherebhajanais performed.   Five statues of Viṣṇu, Bhīmasena and Mahākāla are installed on the western wall of thephalcā. Two of the statues (one of Viṣṇu and one of Bhīmasena) are made of wood whilst the others have been carved from stone.The five-bayeddalāna-esquephalcāoriginally had only one floor, but was later reconstructed as a three-storiedsataḥ. In 2016, it was rebuilt with the support of the Lalitpur Municipality and the Indian Embassy. None of the historical wooden elements were used in the reconstruction.
description_ne: यो भिन्द्यः सत्तः भिन्द्यःलाछि चोकमा  च्यासल (उत्तर)बाट वल्खु (दक्षिण) तिर जाने बाटोको पश्चिमपट्टि रहेको छ । यो सत्तः धौबजि फल्चाको पश्चिमपट्टि र भीमसेन मन्दिर एवं इनारको उत्तरपट्टि रहेको छ । फल्चामा रहेको शिलालेखमा दिइएको जानकारी अनुसार यो फल्चा निर्माण गरेर भीमसेनलाई चढाइएको थियो । पाँच वटा कवल भएको दलान जस्तो देखिने यो फल्चा पहिला भुइँतले मात्र थियो, तर पछि यसलाई तीनतले सत्तःको रूपमा पुनर्निर्माण गरियो । त्यसपछि सन् २०१६ मा ललितपुर नगरपालिका र भारतीय राजदूतावासको कार्यालयको सहयोगमा पुराना ऐतिहासिक काठहरूको कत्ति पनि प्रयोग नगरी पुनर्निर्माण गरियो ।

Details Transliteration of the stone inscription of Bhindyaḥlāchi Capāḥ Phalcā (transcribed by Nutan Sharma , 2018) [Svasti sign] śrī bhīmasenāya namaḥ || mārggāṇāṃ vighnahantāraṃ dāṇuvāraṃ siromaṇi || Kauravāḥ māra saṃhārā- rtamvande draupadipriyaṃ || svasti || samvatsara 871 phālguṇa māse śukla pakṣe || tṛtīyāyāṃntithau utatra bhādra pra revatī nakṣetre || śubha varaśika yoge tetilagaraṇe | yathā mūharttake || ādi- tavāsare || kumbha rāśigate savitari|| mīnarāśigate candramasi || tasmindine śrī matchri śrībhīmase- na pritina nhapā dasya cogva phale jīrṇa juyāva coṅasa bauddhagītakṛta dhamma dyakā guru thāpanā dhuṅā _ _ kula bhāro, lakṣmīsiṃha bhāvo, kajhita khapiṃche nāyhiti phusa gṛha prajāpati gyānasiṃha prajāpati bhā- gīrathasiṃ bhāvo sisiṃha prajāpati sūryyasiṃha prajāpati mukundasiṃha prajāpati dhantasiṃha prajā- pati bidhusiṃha prajāpati anantasiṃha prajāpati dhanaśaṃkara prajāpati puna dharmasiṃha prajāpa- ti masiṃ prajāptī dhamarā prajāptī aṣchi prajaptī kajitayā bhāryyā sūryyalakṣmīmayi bhitri thavte smuhana thva pata- kvalāchisa thva śata dayakaṃ pratiṣṭhā [yā]ṅā drinna juro || puna bhākhā sa eva gyānasiṃha pramukhana jimanhasamha samuhana mohora ṭaṃkā ṣuyacyā 68 dantā thva dānayā kalatrana śrībuṃgayātayā raṃgana yāta ṅhāva kunhu thva satarasa cāṃgva depva pujāyāsya phaṃ 1 siyāvaji phaṃ 2 ajithvaṃ dhaṃ 12 rābu 1 chāta thvateyā cettayāta dānabisyaṃ pra 2 ceknayā mata choke māra bhūya indrajātrā lhugla yāta kunu deva pūjā dana biya mata chvayeke nejyātasaṃ utiṃ yāya māra juro | thvateyā cittāyāka sa- eva gyānasiṃha ādina jimanhasa mha samuhasa avichinna yāsyaṃ cintā yāya  [mā]ra || puna bhākhā thva śatana phale suṃ jogi dopa phogiṃ taya madu gomhanaṃ tavasā paṃñca mahāpātaka rā- ka juro || || śrī 3 bhīmasenaya kudṛṣti rāka juro || śubhamastu || : || māra deva citāka juro (On top of the inscription is a small statue of Lord Buddha) Provisional Translation: Salutations to the venerable Bhīmasena, remover of obstacles, the jewel of head (ornament). Salutations to him who killed the Kauravas and who is Draupadī's beloved one. May all be well. In the year of (NS) 871 (1751 CE), on the third day of bright fortnight of Phālguna, on the constellation of Uttara Bhādra and Revati, subha-yoga , Teliya Karaṇa, Sunday when the sun is in Aquarius and the moon in Pisces. On this day, the decayed rest house which was built in devotion to Bhīmasen was renovated as a sataḥ by the group of Kula Bhāro, Lakṣmīsiṃha Bhāro, Gyānasiṃha Prajāpati who is the senior member lives near Khapinche, Nayhiti, Prajāpati Bhāgīrathasiṃ Bhāvo, Sisiṃha Prajāpati, Sūryyasiṃha Prajāpati, Mukundasiṃha Prajāpati, Dhantasiṃha Prajāpati, Bidhusiṃha Prajāpati, Anantasiṃha Prajāpati, Dhanaśaṃkara Prajāpati, Dharmasiṃha Prajāpati, Masiṃ Prajāpati, Dhamarā Prajāpati, Aṣchi Prajāpati, Sūryyalakṣmīmayi who is the wife of senior member after establishing the Caryā Guṭhī and a guru (in it). Again, the same group of 17 persons led by Gyānasiṃha Prajāpati offers 68 mohor coins to worship the deities of the phalcā by making a dāna of burning wick lamp with four mānās of oil during the festivals of Indrajātrā and Rāto (red) Matsyendranātha Lagana-jātrā after offering 1 pāthī (?), puffed rice 2 pāthī , 12 daṃ of rice beer and one type of meat. For both, the same amount (of offering) shall be made. The responsible persons are the same group of 17 persons led by Gyānasiṃha Prajāpati. Again, it is not allowed to give shelter to a jogī (Kapālī), dopa (do͂) and phogiṃ (begger) in the phale . If allowed by anybody, he shall get five kinds of great sin (killing a woman, brahman, cow etc.) and shall bear the anger of the three times venerable Bhīmasen. May all be well.

historical_events.event_description: A group of Avāles led by Kula Bhāro and Lakṣmīsiṃha Bhāro built thesataḥafter dismantling an oldphalcāat this site in 1751 CE. They also donated 68mohorcoins (mohara-rūpaiyā) to finance its upkeep.
Lalitpur Municipality donated 12,000 Nepalese Rupees and ca. 25,000 Nepalese Rupees were collected from local donors for the restoration of thesataḥ.

Thesataḥwas rebuilt with support from the Bhindyaḥlāchi Ṭola Sudhāra Samiti, the Lalitpura Vikāsko Lāgi Samāja, the Indian Embassy, and the Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan City. The Indian Embassy donated 5,985,000 Nepali Rupees and local donations amounted to about 1,000,000 Nepali Rupees. Thesataḥ wasinaugurated on 2 July 2016 CE by H.E. Shri Ranjit Rae, the Indian ambassador to Nepal.
